```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Transportation_Problem")
    m.setParam("TimeLimit", 300)  # Set time limit to 300 seconds

    # Data
    sources = list(range(4))  # S0..S3
    destinations = list(range(10))  # D0..D9

    supplies = [186, 129, 173, 189]
    demands = [65, 74, 60, 18, 64, 31, 72, 30, 25, 46]

    # Cost matrix: rows correspond to sources S0..S3, columns to destinations D0..D9
    costs = [
        [ 19.74,  16.64,  16.47,  23.45,  12.45,  12.37,  23.91,  19.45,  24.12,  25.02],  # S0
        [  5.77,  28.26,  28.25,  12.35,   6.35,  16.30,  19.73,  15.41,  16.60,  15.94],  # S1
        [ 18.88,  13.63,  25.21,  12.66,  27.54,  19.26,  26.66,  17.76,  14.42,  13.15],  # S2
        [ 21.16,  16.91,  10.04,   8.37,  26.43,  13.34,  28.56,  21.04,  11.75,  16.55],  # S3
    ]

    # Decision variables:
    # Flow_S{i}_D{j} >= 0 is the quantity shipped from source i to destination j
    flows = {}
    for i in sources:
        for j in destinations:
            flows[(i, j)] = m.addVar(lb=0.0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Flow_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Objective: Minimize total transportation cost
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(costs[i][j] * flows[(i, j)] for i in sources for j in destinations),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Supply constraints: Shipments from each source <= its supply
    for i in sources:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for j in destinations) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}"
        )

    # Demand constraints: Shipments to each destination >= its demand
    for j in destinations:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for i in sources) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}"
        )

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Leadership Team
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: [Insert Date]
Subject: Cost-Effective Shipping Plan Across Our Network

Situation:
We need to move finished goods from multiple warehouses and plants to a broad set of stores, customers, and regional hubs. Transportation spend is under pressure due to varying carrier rates by lane, while our service standards require on-time, in-full deliveries. Getting this right reduces costs, prevents stockouts, and protects customer satisfaction. The attached shipping data summarizes available inventory at each origin, required quantities at each destination, and route-level shipping costs across our network.

Problem:
We must decide how much to ship from each source to each destination, recognizing that each origin has limited inventory and each destination has a firm requirement. Shipping costs differ by route, so the choice of origin for each destination materially affects total spend. Partial shipments are allowed, including splitting a destination’s requirement across multiple sources when that lowers cost or supports service.

Goal:
- Meet the required quantity at every destination without exceeding available inventory at any source
- Use the route-level cost differences to allocate shipments in a way that drives total shipping cost as low as possible
- Maintain service reliability by selecting feasible lanes and shipment patterns, noting that partial shipments are permitted

Upon review and confirmation of the attached data, we will prepare a recommended shipment plan that specifies flows from each origin to each destination. We will align with transportation procurement and operations to execute, monitor performance, and adjust as conditions change.

Annex – Shipping Data:
Destination requirements: Store D6 needs 72 units; Store D3 needs 18 units; Store D0 needs 65 units; Store D2 needs 60 units; Store D8 needs 25 units; Store D1 needs 74 units; Store D5 needs 31 units; Store D7 needs 30 units; Store D9 needs 46 units; Store D4 needs 64 units.
